# The Formation of New Beliefs
  ¶2 UNCOVERED: Time and space, cause and effect, nature and history, and one's own biography remain untouched.
  ¶3 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): THE POINT I NOW URGE YOU TO OBSERVE PARTICULARLY IS the part played by the older truths.
  ¶3 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): Failure to take account of IT is the source of much of the unjust criticism leveled against pragmatism.
  ¶4 UNCOVERED: You doubtless wish examples of this process of truth's growth, and the only trouble is their superabundance.
  ¶5 UNCOVERED: If I should now utter piercing shrieks and act like a maniac on this platform, it would make many of you revise your ideas as to the probable worth of my philosophy.
  ¶5 UNCOVERED: 'Radium' came the other day as part of the day's content, and seemed for a moment to contradict our ideas of the whole order of nature, that order having come to be identified with what is called the conservation of energy.
  ¶5 UNCOVERED: The mere sight of radium paying heat away indefinitely out of its own pocket seemed to violate that conservation.
  ¶5 UNCOVERED: What to think?
  ¶5 UNCOVERED: If the radiations from it were nothing but an escape of unsuspected 'potential' energy, pre-existent inside of the atoms, the principle of conservation would be saved.
  ¶5 UNCOVERED: The discovery of 'helium' as the radiation's outcome, opened a way to this belief.
  ¶5 UNCOVERED: So Ramsay's view is generally held to be true, because, altho it extends our old ideas of energy, it causes a minimum of alteration in their nature.
  ¶6 UNCOVERED: I need not multiply instances.
  ¶6 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): It must both lean on old truth and grasp new fact; and its success (AS I SAID A MOMENT AGO) in doing this, is a matter for the individual's appreciation.
  ¶9 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): Mr. Schiller still gives to all this view of truth the name of 'Humanism,' but, for this doctrine too, the name of pragmatism seems fairly to be in the ascendant, SO I WILL TREAT IT UNDER THE NAME OF PRAGMATISM IN THESE LECTURES.
  ¶10 UNCOVERED: And these two things must be our future topics.
